observation_summary: The SerializationUtils.clone method fails with a ClassNotFoundException when attempting to clone primitive types (e.g., int.class) because the custom ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream does not correctly resolve primitive class names.
hypothesis: The resolveClass method in ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream lacks the logic to handle primitive types, which are not found via standard Class.forName lookups. The fix requires adding a lookup mechanism for primitive types to ensure they are correctly resolved during deserialization.
prediction: The code will be updated to include a mapping of primitive type names to their corresponding Class objects, and the resolveClass method will be modified to check this map when standard class loading fails.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows the addition of a primitiveTypes map and logic in resolveClass to check this map if Class.forName fails. This confirms that the original algorithm for resolving classes was incomplete for primitive types.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an algorithmic failure in the class resolution procedure. The existing logic only attempted to load classes via ClassLoader, which is insufficient for primitive types. The fix implements a more robust resolution algorithm by adding a fallback lookup for primitive types, which is a procedural correction to the class resolution logic.
evidence_used: The bug report states that SerializationUtils throws ClassNotFoundException when cloning primitive classes.
The fix diff shows the addition of a primitiveTypes map and a lookup mechanism in resolveClass.
The stack trace shows the failure occurs in resolveClass during deserialization.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a check (if cls != null), the root cause is the absence of a mechanism to resolve primitive types, which is a procedural/algorithmic deficiency in the class resolution strategy.
